docs.explain: Mean and median both answer what is typical by size. MODE answers what is typical by frequency, which is a different question and the right one whenever the values are categories wearing numbers: shoe sizes, ticket sizes, pack counts, the number of boxes a shop orders. The answer is a value that actually occurs, which is why a mode is easy to explain to a room and a mean often is not. Two limits matter. A list where every value occurs once has no mode at all, and Excel says `#N/A` rather than inventing one. A list with two equally frequent values is also ambiguous: classic MODE returns the one that appears first in the data, while the newer MODE.MULT returns all of them, so a tie is a decision you should make explicitly rather than inherit. MODE ignores blanks and text, counts only numbers, and will not tell you how often the mode occurs — pair it with COUNTIF when the frequency itself belongs in the report.
